evidence.excerpt: The Serbian Medicines and Medical Devices Agency has been developing a plain-language standard for summary of product characteristics documents since 2021. This study reports the formal evaluation of a draft standard applied to 40 test documents (20 prescription, 20 over-the-counter medicines). Eight raters from different professional backgrounds (pharmacists, medical writers, patient representatives, and psychologists) scored each document on a 30-item adherence checklist based on the draft standard. Intraclass correlation coefficients for the total adherence score were ICC(2,1) = 0.81, indicating good inter-rater reliability. Stakeholder focus groups (n = 24 participants across three groups) identified that the provisions on numerical risk expression were considered the most beneficial by patient representatives but the most burdensome to implement by regulatory affairs professionals. Revisions to two sections of the draft standard are recommended based on combined quantitative and qualitative findings.
